title: Failure-only collection of the owned Windows startup trace

checkpoint.kind: reviewed immutable source objects; combined integration and native execution pending

nativeContract.divisionOfReview: This file documents only the collector and its agreement with the fixed native contract. The native-source-review, native-edit-manifest, protocol and native-review-checks files document the separate header change.

motivation.observedFailure: The completed fc901 Windows native execution compiled and deployed, but the owned application exited before the first-window observation with access violation 0xc0000005. The retained outcome did not establish a faulting function or a COM/property-bag ownership defect.
motivation.change: Collect the native trace only after an existing failure and existing cleanup. The trace can identify retained source boundaries; it does not itself identify the corrupting/faulting call or establish a startup repair.

changes: Add a bounded C# helper to the existing Add-Type block for exact process identity checks, one fixed source-file read, exclusive artifact retention and strict flat ASCII JSONL validation.
Add one PowerShell helper that produces only typed fixed metadata and selected validated rows.
Initialize a failure flag and borrowed IntPtr; retain the result of the one existing Process.Handle access at its original position before saved StartTime acquisition.
Set the failure flag immediately after the original primary ErrorRecord assignment.
Invoke collection only at the end of the original finally, after retained-process cleanup, drag-trace retention, WER restoration and crash receipt.

protected: Original process-stop and drag-trace retention order
Existing failure diagnostics and ErrorRecord rethrow

portabilityRefinement.description: Replace HashSet<string> with a fixed string[] and Array.IndexOf for exact closed membership. This avoids relying on an implicit System.Core compiler reference; no compiler failure was observed here.

processAndPathBinding.borrowedHandle: The original Handle query result is retained while the Process object remains held. The collector never reopens a PID or closes that borrowed process handle.
processAndPathBinding.confirmation: GetProcessId and GetProcessTimes must match the saved PID and round-trip UTC StartTime, including full 100 ns FILETIME precision. A zero-time WaitForSingleObject must confirm the process exited; Stop-Process completion alone is not used as evidence.
processAndPathBinding.sourceRevision: Exactly the lowercase 40-hex GITHUB_SHA observed by the smoke script.
processAndPathBinding.resolver: Parent GetTempPathW(MAX_PATH + 1), no fallback/search, combined UTF-16 path length strictly below MAX_PATH.
processAndPathBinding.unknowns: Unconfirmed identity or exit prevents file access. Parent and child temp environments may differ; a missing file does not prove Configure was not entered.

retention.source: One fixed disk file opened read-only without write/delete sharing, rejecting directory/reparse attributes and mismatched final handle path. Size is at most 16,384 bytes; EOF, identity, size, creation/write metadata and link count are checked around the read.
retention.afterClose: Bytes and SHA-256 are exposed only after the owned source read handle closes. This is a stable read-time snapshot, not a claim of uninterrupted pathname identity after closure.
retention.exclusive: CreateNew only under existing OutDir; no overwrite, retry or deletion. Raw bytes are flushed, read back and closed before row projection is allowed. A failed write may leave a partial new artifact but is never reported retained.
retention.wholeHash: The raw SHA-256 covers all bytes of the bounded complete source-file snapshot, including an incomplete final JSONL record if present. It is not a hash of the selected console subset.
retention.malformed: Unknown/duplicate keys, wrong types, noncanonical identity, foreign complete rows, invalid sequence, non-ASCII, row/byte cap violations and records after trace-limit suppress all row projection.
retention.partialTail: All exact bytes remain retained. Only a fully validated preceding row prefix may be projected, with partialTailBytes and recordStreamComplete=false. Empty files have status empty-file and unknown stream completeness.

projection.selection: First eight and last sixteen complete validated rows, without duplication; at most 24 with explicit omissions.
projection.publicFields: Fixed source revision, PID, decimal creation FILETIME, statuses, booleans/null, numeric counts/error codes, raw-byte SHA, fixed artifact names and exact closed stage labels. No raw paths, exception text, process strings, credentials or arbitrary row content.
projection.overflow: A fixed output-limit envelope declares outputByteLimit=8192; it does not manufacture a pass or complete trace.
projection.secondaryErrors: Collector, retention, JSON and console errors stay inside guarded diagnostic paths and cannot replace the original primary ErrorRecord.
projection.interpretation: No finalized native footer; a complete JSONL file is not proof that startup completed. The contention boolean is known only through that row. Missing returned markers may reflect an earlier guard/exception, omitted trace, cap or write failure rather than a callee that never returned. Tracing and synchronous IO can perturb timing and have no guaranteed wall-time bound.

author.scope: Six source/portable contract/model designs only; no PowerShell parser, C# compiler, .NET/Win32 IO, process, UIA or native execution.
groups: Exact source identities, six inverses, protected actions/error/cleanup order and fixed API/vocabulary contracts
Portable owned-handle identity and fixed-path contract, exact FILETIME strings and unknown exit states
Portable strict ASCII JSONL model: canonical identity, exact types/keys, malformed suppression, partial tails and record limits
Deterministic stable-read/close/hash and exclusive-retention models, unavailable ownership and IO failures
Portable typed projection, deterministic omissions, raw-byte binding and complete CRLF envelope limits
Explicit non-PowerShell lifecycle model: failure-only placement, original Error identity and cleanup isolation
